page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is a compute-focused virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is bundled with 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core compute capabilities alongside consistent mid-tier multi-threaded processing. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves a top-quartile single-core score of 2,938.58 and a multi-core score of 23,323.12. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1,727.0 and a multi-core score of 8,968.0, with dedicated sub-tests reaching 12,769.0 for software compilation and 14,270.0 for ray tracing. In-memory and caching operations remain stable, demonstrated by Redis write performance reaching 15.55 million operations per second and static web serving throughput hitting 9.41 GB/sec.

Resource tradeoffs center on the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU distribution and hardware instruction constraints. While the processor supports AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. In large language model tests, small 135M parameter inference runs at 1,045.11 prompt tokens per second, but 7B model prompt processing drops into the lower quartile at 25.18 tokens per second due to memory density and instruction limits.

This hardware balance offers cost-effective execution for compute-bound tasks that do not require extensive RAM footprints. Suitable workloads include continuous integration pipelines, software build farms, batch processing workers, static web servers, and mid-tier backend microservices.
description: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture. The virtual machine delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no discrete GPU acceleration. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration targets compute-dense tasks over memory-heavy workloads. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-thread CPU performance in stress-ng tests, balanced multi-core execution in Geekbench, and consistent memory operations with 15.55 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware limits include the absence of AVX-512 extensions and constrained RAM capacity, which limits heavier LLM inference efficiency. The instance provides a practical compute-focused foundation for CI/CD compilation, batch workloads, web serving, and backend application hosting.
